chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani from Sulayman ibn Hafsh al-Marwazi who said:

Abu al-Hasan (the Last Imam), peace be upon him, said: 'Beware of sleeping between the Night Prayer and the Dawn Prayer, but rather take a short rest without deep sleep, for the one who does so is not praised for what he has offered of his prayer.'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'When the dawn rises and becomes distinct, let him call the Adhan until he reaches the phrase [implied context], then let him raise his head and remember God until the sun rises. All of this has been explained in the summary of what preceded. Then he said (may God have mercy on him): 'Then let him raise his head and remember God frequently until the sun rises,' until the end of the chapter.'

key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: The Sheikh (referring to Al-Shaykh al-Tusi or Al-Shaykh al-Mufid in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sleeping between the Night Prayer and Dawn Prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that deep sleep between the Night Prayer and Dawn Prayer nullifies the spiritual merit of the preceding worship, recommending instead a state of light dozing (qada'a) to maintain spiritual alertness. Al-Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by linking the post-dawn remembrance to the prophetic practice of delaying the Fajr Adhan until the light is distinct, emphasizing the continuity of devotion from dawn until sunrise.
